# package uadp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/uadp"
```

Package uadp implements the UADP message mapping of OPC UA PubSub (Part 14 §7.2.2 in 1.04, §7.2.4 in 1.05): the binary encoding of NetworkMessages and DataSetMessages, including the message security of the security header.

#### Wire layout {#hdr-Wire_layout}

A NetworkMessage is laid out as

	UADPFlags | ExtendedFlags1 | ExtendedFlags2 | PublisherId | DataSetClassId
	GroupHeader | PayloadHeader | Timestamp | PicoSeconds | PromotedFields
	SecurityHeader | Payload | SecurityFooter | Signature

Which optional parts are present follows [message.NetworkMessage.UADPMask](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#NetworkMessage.UADPMask) and [message.DataSetMessage.UADPMask](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#DataSetMessage.UADPMask) on encode; Decode reports what it found in the same masks. ExtendedFlags1 and ExtendedFlags2 are only written when one of their bits is needed, exactly as open62541 does.

#### Security {#hdr-Security}

With SecurityMode Sign the signature covers the whole message from the UADPFlags up to and including the SecurityFooter. With SignAndEncrypt the Payload and the SecurityFooter are encrypted first (in place, AES-CTR keeps the length) with the MessageNonce of the security header, and the signature is then computed over the encrypted message. This is the layout of open62541 (src/pubsub/ua\_pubsub\_writergroup.c, encryptAndSign; readergroup.c, verifyAndDecryptNetworkMessage). The codec is independent of the policy: it only calls the [security.Policy](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/security#Policy) methods.

#### Chunks {#hdr-Chunks}

A DataSetMessage or a discovery announcement too large for one NetworkMessage is sent as chunk NetworkMessages (Part 14 §7.2.4.4.4 in 1.05, ExtendedFlags2 bit 0): [EncodeChunks](#func-encodechunks) splits it, every chunk secured on its own. Decode returns a chunk with [message.NetworkMessage.Chunk](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#NetworkMessage.Chunk) set, after its security was checked; a [Reassembler](#type-reassembler) collects the chunks within bounded memory and [DecodeReassembled](#func-decodereassembled) decodes the complete message. The layout is that of the OPC Foundation .NET stack 2.x (UadpChunker, UadpReassembler); open62541 1.5.9 neither sends nor accepts chunks.

#### Discovery {#hdr-Discovery}

Discovery probes (NetworkMessage type 1, [message.DiscoveryRequest](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#DiscoveryRequest)) and announcements (type 2, [message.Discovery](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#Discovery)) of Part 14 §7.2.4.6 in 1.05 are encoded and decoded in the layout of the spec or of the .NET stack 2.x ([message.DiscoveryLayout](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#DiscoveryLayout)); Decode recognises both. The ActionResponder and ActionMetaData announcements of PubSub Actions are not supported.

#### Actions {#hdr-Actions}

The ActionRequest and ActionResponse NetworkMessages of PubSub Actions (Part 14 §6.2.11.2 and Tables 154, 166 and 167 in 1.05) are DataSet NetworkMessages with [message.NetworkMessage.Action](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/message#NetworkMessage.Action) set: the ActionHeader (bit 5 of ExtendedFlags2) follows the security header and is secured with the payload, the DataSetMessages are of type ActionRequest or ActionResponse. [PeekAction](#func-peekaction) recognises them without decoding.

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrFiltered is returned by Decode when the Accept callback rejected
	// the message after its header was decoded.
	ErrFiltered = errors.New("pubsub/uadp: message filtered")
	// ErrMalformed is returned for a message that does not follow the
	// UADP encoding, and by Encode for a NetworkMessage that cannot be
	// encoded.
	ErrMalformed = errors.New("pubsub/uadp: malformed message")
	// ErrUnsupported is returned for valid UADP features this package does
	// not implement (discovery messages of PubSub Actions, reserved
	// DataSetMessage types).
	ErrUnsupported = errors.New("pubsub/uadp: unsupported")
	// ErrSecurityMode is returned by Decode when the security of a message
	// is weaker than required, or when a secured message arrives and no
	// keys are available to verify it.
	ErrSecurityMode = errors.New("pubsub/uadp: security mode rejected")
	// ErrSecurityChecksFailed is returned by Decode for an invalid security
	// header, a bad signature or a failed decryption, and by Encode when
	// signing or encryption fails.
	ErrSecurityChecksFailed = errors.New("pubsub/uadp: security checks failed")
	// ErrNoMetaData is returned by Decode for a RawData DataSetMessage
	// whose DataSetMetaData the MetaData callback does not supply: RawData
	// fields carry no type information.
	ErrNoMetaData = errors.New("pubsub/uadp: RawData needs the DataSetMetaData")
)
```

Errors returned by Encode and Decode. They are wrapped with details; test with errors.Is.

```go
var ErrChunkRejected = errors.New("pubsub/uadp: chunk rejected")
```

ErrChunkRejected is returned by [Reassembler.Add](#func-reassembler-add) for a chunk it discards: one outside its message, of a size the layout of the message does not allow, a duplicate, one of a message beyond the limits, or one there is no room for. It is wrapped with the reason.

## Functions

### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte, opts *DecodeOptions) (*message.NetworkMessage, error)
```

Decode decodes a NetworkMessage. It never modifies b; the returned message does not reference b. A chunk is returned with nm.Chunk set and, for a DataSetMessage chunk, nm.Messages holding the DataSetWriterId of its PayloadHeader; pass it to a [Reassembler](#type-reassembler).

### func DecodeReassembled

```go
func DecodeReassembled(header *message.NetworkMessage, payload []byte, opts *DecodeOptions) (*message.NetworkMessage, error)
```

DecodeReassembled decodes the message reassembled from the chunks of header, a chunk NetworkMessage returned by Decode: the DataSetMessage of its writer, or the discovery announcement. The headers, security included, are those of header; its security was checked chunk by chunk. Only opts.MetaData is used. The returned NetworkMessage has no Chunk.

### func Encode

```go
func Encode(nm *message.NetworkMessage, opts *EncodeOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode encodes a NetworkMessage.

A NetworkMessage of type NetworkMessageDataSet needs at least one DataSetMessage, and the PayloadHeader when it has more than one. A NetworkMessage of type NetworkMessageDiscoveryResponse carries nm.Discovery, one of type NetworkMessageDiscoveryRequest nm.Request; the PayloadHeader bit of the mask is ignored for them. With nm.Chunk set Encode writes that one chunk: the PayloadHeader is then the DataSetWriterId of the single DataSetMessage of nm. The WriterGroupId, GroupVersion, NetworkMessageNumber and SequenceNumber bits only take effect together with the GroupHeader bit. nm.Security is ignored: the security header follows from opts. Encode does not modify nm.

For a secured message the caller increments opts.NonceSequence for every message; MessageNonces must never repeat for the same keys, since AES-CTR with a repeated counter block reveals the plaintext.

### func EncodeChunks

```go
func EncodeChunks(nm *message.NetworkMessage, opts *EncodeOptions, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error)
```

EncodeChunks encodes nm as chunk NetworkMessages of at most maxSize bytes each, security included. nm is a NetworkMessage of type NetworkMessageDataSet with exactly one DataSetMessage (an action message too), or a discovery announcement; discovery probes are not chunked. Use it for a NetworkMessage that Encode makes larger than maxSize.

The MessageSequenceNumber of the chunks is the low 16 bits of the SequenceNumber of the DataSetMessage, or the SequenceNumber of the announcement. Chunk i carries the GroupHeader SequenceNumber and NetworkMessageNumber of nm plus i: the caller advances its counters by the number of chunks. A secured chunk takes its MessageNonce from opts.NextNonceSequenceForToken or opts.NextNonceSequence, or from opts.NonceSequence plus i.


PeekAction reports whether an encoded UADP NetworkMessage is an action message (bit 5 of ExtendedFlags2), without decoding it.

### func PeekType

```go
func PeekType(b []byte) (t message.NetworkMessageType, chunk bool, err error)
```

PeekType returns the NetworkMessage type of an encoded UADP NetworkMessage from its flags, without decoding it, and whether it is a chunk.

### type DecodeOptions

```go
type DecodeOptions struct {
	// Accept, if set, is called with the decoded NetworkMessage header
	// (publisher id, group header, payload header, security header)
	// before the payload is verified, decrypted and decoded. Returning
	// false stops decoding with ErrFiltered. The DataSetMessages of the
	// header carry only their DataSetWriterID; the Action of an action
	// message is set but still empty (the ActionHeader follows the
	// security header).
	Accept func(header *message.NetworkMessage) bool
	// Security returns the security mode the receiver requires for a
	// message and the keys to verify and decrypt it. It is called after
	// Accept. Nil, or a nil KeySource, accepts only unsecured messages.
	Security func(header *message.NetworkMessage) (ua.MessageSecurityMode, security.KeySource, error)
	// MetaData supplies the DataSetMetaData needed to decode RawData
	// fields and to name fields. Without a PayloadHeader the
	// DataSetWriterId is unknown and passed as 0.
	MetaData message.MetaDataLookup
}
```

### type EncodeOptions

```go
type EncodeOptions struct {
	// SecurityMode is None (or Invalid) for an unsecured message, Sign or
	// SignAndEncrypt. Keys must be set for the latter two.
	SecurityMode ua.MessageSecurityMode
	Keys         security.KeySource
	// NonceSequence is the sender's message counter used to build unique
	// MessageNonces; the caller increments it for every secured message.
	NonceSequence uint32
	// NextNonceSequence, if set, replaces NonceSequence: it is called for
	// every secured NetworkMessage Encode and EncodeChunks build (each
	// chunk is secured on its own) and returns a new counter value.
	NextNonceSequence func() uint32
	// NextNonceSequenceForToken, if set, replaces NextNonceSequence: it
	// is called like it with the SecurityTokenId of the keys the message
	// is secured with, so that the sender can start its counter at 1
	// again for a new token (Part 14 §7.2.4.4.3.2 Table 156).
	NextNonceSequenceForToken func(tokenID uint32) uint32
	// MetaData supplies the DataSetMetaData of RawData DataSetMessages:
	// the MaxStringLength padding of String and ByteString fields, the
	// number of array dimensions and their upper bounds. Without it,
	// RawData fields are written as their values are typed and sized.
	MetaData message.MetaDataLookup
}
```

EncodeOptions control Encode.

### type Reassembler

```go
type Reassembler struct {

	// of *reasmEntry, oldest first

}
```

Reassembler reassembles chunked NetworkMessages. Chunks are kept per PublisherId, WriterGroupId, DataSetWriterId, NetworkMessage type, security mode, SecurityTokenId and MessageSequenceNumber; the chunks of a message may arrive in any order and interleaved with those of other messages. Chunks that cannot belong to one message discard it: a chunk for a slot that holds other data, and, when the chunks carry the GroupHeader SequenceNumber or NetworkMessageNumber, numbers that neither are the same in every chunk nor advance by one per chunk. It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewReassembler

```go
func NewReassembler(opts *ReassemblerOptions) *Reassembler
```

NewReassembler returns a Reassembler with the given limits (nil: the defaults).

#### func (Reassembler) Add

```go
func (r *Reassembler) Add(nm *message.NetworkMessage, now time.Time) (payload []byte, dropped int, err error)
```

Add adds a chunk NetworkMessage returned by Decode, received at now. It returns the reassembled message, to be decoded with DecodeReassembled, once the chunk completes it, and nil while chunks are missing. A chunk it discards returns an error wrapping ErrChunkRejected. dropped is the number of chunks of incomplete messages Add dropped because they expired or to make room. The returned payload does not reference nm.

#### func (Reassembler) Expire

```go
func (r *Reassembler) Expire(now time.Time) int
```

Expire drops the incomplete messages that waited longer than the Timeout at now and returns the number of their chunks. Add expires messages as well; Expire releases their memory when no chunks arrive.

#### func (Reassembler) Reset

```go
func (r *Reassembler) Reset()
```

Reset drops all incomplete messages. It does not count them.

### type ReassemblerOptions

```go
type ReassemblerOptions struct {
	// MaxMessageSize is the largest TotalSize accepted (default 2 MiB).
	MaxMessageSize int
	// MaxChunks is the largest number of chunks of one message (default
	// 8192): it bounds the bookkeeping of tiny chunks.
	MaxChunks int
	// MaxPendingMessages and MaxPendingBytes limit the incomplete
	// messages of all publishers (default 512 and 32 MiB).
	MaxPendingMessages int
	MaxPendingBytes    int
	// MaxPublisherMessages and MaxPublisherBytes limit the incomplete
	// messages of one PublisherId (default 64 and 8 MiB). They are raised
	// to what one message of MaxMessageSize needs.
	MaxPublisherMessages int
	MaxPublisherBytes    int
	// Timeout is how long an incomplete message waits for its missing
	// chunks, counted from its first chunk (default 5 seconds).
	Timeout time.Duration
}
```

ReassemblerOptions bound the memory of a [Reassembler](#type-reassembler). Zero values select the defaults. Chunks arrive unauthenticated if the messages are not secured: the limits keep a sender from making the receiver hold more than MaxPendingBytes, and a single PublisherId from taking more than its share. Every stored chunk is charged its size plus a fixed 64 bytes.
